title: Salted honey tart
subtitle: honey custard in a crisp shortcrust, finished with flaky sea salt
excerpt: Salted honey tart is a smooth, amber honey custard baked in a blind-baked shortcrust case, finished with flaky sea salt. The filling has four ingredients: honey, double cream, eggs, and vanilla. The honey flavour comes through cleanly against the custard base. Use a honey with some character, such as a wildflower or heather variety; a very neutral honey produces a flat, sweet filling with no depth.
sourceNotes: Honey custard tarts are documented in European baking from the medieval period onward. The salted honey version with flaky salt as a finish became popular in British and American artisan baking from the 2010s onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: Baking a pastry case without filling, using baking paper and baking beans as a weight to keep the pastry flat. Pre-baked until dry before a wet filling is added.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tart keeps at room temperature, lightly covered, for up to 2 days. Add the sea salt only just before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: fan 130 degrees C / gas 2, for the custard

content.text: Salted honey tart is a four-ingredient custard filling baked low and slow in a

shortcrust case. The custard sets to a smooth, glossy surface with a slight wobble at the centre. Bake at 150 degrees C or lower; too hot and the custard will curdle and puff. Flaky salt goes on just before serving.

items.prepNote: a flavourful variety such as wildflower or heather

content.text: Make the pastry: rub cold butter into flour and icing sugar until crumbly. Add egg yolk and press into a dough. Chill 30 minutes. Roll to 3 mm and line a 22 cm tart tin. Chill 20 minutes.

Heat oven to 190 degrees C (fan 170 degrees C / gas 5). Blind-bake with baking paper and beans for 15 minutes, remove paper and beans, bake a further 10 minutes until the base is pale golden and fully dry. Reduce the oven to 150 degrees C (fan 130 degrees C / gas 2).
Warm the honey and double cream together in a small saucepan until the honey dissolves into the cream; do not boil. Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and vanilla together in a bowl. Pour in the warm cream mixture slowly, whisking as you go. Strain through a sieve into a jug to remove any egg strands.

Place the pastry case on a baking sheet on the oven shelf. Pour the custard into the case carefully (pouring on the shelf avoids spillage from moving the filled case). Bake for 28 to 35 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble at the very centre.
Leave to cool completely in the tin, at least 1 hour. Scatter with flaky sea salt just before serving.

attrs.problem: Custard bubbles and puffs in the oven
attrs.avoid: Avoid baking at too high a temperature; custard curdles and expands at high heat.
attrs.fix: Reduce the oven to 140 degrees C (fan 120 degrees C / gas 1) if the custard is bubbling. The tart will take longer but will set to a smooth, glossy surface.

attrs.problem: Surface of the custard has a skin or wrinkles
attrs.avoid: Avoid cooling the tart in a draughty spot or moving it while still warm.
attrs.fix: Cool the tart in the turned-off oven with the door slightly ajar for the first 20 minutes, then move to a rack. This prevents a sharp temperature change that can wrinkle the surface.
